scope: Twenty-two sentence-audited non-headword Njihov-/njihov- possessive tokens in the base papers.
choice: Replace every audited adjectival Njihov-/njihov- form with the official preferred indeclinable third-person plural possessive Jih/jih, preserving sentence-initial capitalization.
motivation: Official Interslavic grammar says the genitive personal-pronoun possessives jego, jej and jih are the most common third-person forms and are not inflected. Every mapped site means their; the inherited South-shaped adjectival family is absent as an Interslavic headword and creates an unnecessary mixed paradigm.
alternatives_rejected: Retaining njihov- was rejected because it is absent as an official Interslavic headword and preserves a South-Slavic source-layer family beside established jih.

Normalizing to adjectival jihny- was rejected because the grammar presents it only as an alternative and the dictionary marks it type 2, whereas indeclinable jih is type 1 and explicitly preferred in ordinary usage.
Replacing a wider substring family was rejected; only the exact 22 sentence-audited possessive tokens were admitted.
Using reflexive svoj was rejected because none of the 22 possessors is coreferential with the grammatical subject in the relevant clause.

evidence.official_grammar: Official pronouns.md (10370 bytes, SHA-256 AB4F7B04FD55618DE2EB5FEB282558BEDEC6C205BEBB0E6BBD612CB3FBC88141) lines 48-52 says third-person possessive jih is most common and uninflected; adjectival jihny is an alternative.
evidence.official_dictionary: Official dictionary ID 2601 gives jih, possessive pronoun, type 1, 'their'; ID 6258 gives alternative jihny as type 2. No Njihov-/njihov- Interslavic headword exists.
evidence.cross_family_evidence: The official comparator row for jih bridges West and East forms (Polish ich, Czech jejich, Slovak ich, Belarusian/Russian/Ukrainian іх/их/їх) while retaining Slovene recognition; the removed adjectival surface is concentrated in the South comparators.
evidence.semantic_audit: All 22 sites denote third-person plural possession of a basis, resultant, variety, powers, quotient, invariants, least common multiple, number, meaning, components, structure, automorphism rings, representations or products. There are zero object-pronoun or reflexive-possessive sites.
evidence.protected_domains: No mapped token occurs in a TeX control name, comment, foreign quotation or bibliography identity. Headings and explanatory footnotes containing mapped tokens are editable Interslavic prose.

validation.coverage: The frozen source histogram contains exactly 22 whole-token Njihov-/njihov- possessives over 11 case-sensitive surface forms, all in the base papers.
validation.postcondition: Every mapped adjectival source form is zero; all-source jih/Jih rises from 135 to 157.
validation.structure: Line count, raw brace counts, ordered TeX-control stream and math-delimiter stream are invariant; the other three Latin source files are byte-identical.
validation.reproducibility: The frozen successor was independently calculated and matched the exact bytes/hash before the source patch was admitted.
